output_value: Which release of this field list the row was written under. Filled by the workflow.
The corpus identifier of the source document, such as SRC377.
SHA-256 of the source PDF, binding the row to one binary. A mismatch means the document changed and the extraction is void.
The listed type, such as Financials or PPM. Readers keep the listed type.
The reading group the document belongs to, derived from its type.
CORE, SECONDARY, or REFERENCE. Controls what evidence classes are acceptable and keeps template material out of the fund dataset.
Which blind extractor wrote the row, A or B. Becomes ADJUDICATED on a final row.
What kind of fact this row is, chosen from the closed family list. Follows the table the value sits in, not the document type.
The physical PDF page number the value is printed on.
The kind of layout the value came from: TABLE, FIGURE, NARRATIVE, FORM, FOOTNOTE, SCHEDULE, or DOCUMENT. Always uppercase.
The printed section heading above the table, such as Statements of Financial Position.
The printed table or figure title that names the whole table. Never a date and never a heading that covers only some columns.
The printed row label the value sits on. The primary physical anchor for a value.
The printed column header the value sits under, taken from the lowest header directly above the column. Kept unique within a row, so stacked headers such as 1-Yr Total Return are preserved whole.
Which instance this is when the same row and column labels repeat on one page, counted top to bottom then left to right. Normally 1.
What kind of thing the row measures, in lowercase, from the closed list. Read from the row's own printed label, not decided once per document.
The printed name of the thing being measured: the fund, portfolio, position, asset class, or benchmark named on that row.

The printed asset class governing the row, such as Private Equity or Fixed Income. Taken from the group heading, table title, or document statement that covers the row. A core analytical dimension: fill it whenever the page states it, never infer it, and never restate the row label here.
The printed strategy governing the row, such as Buyout, Venture, or Core Real Estate. Same sourcing rule as asset class.
The printed geographic scope governing the row, such as North America or Europe. Same sourcing rule as asset class.
The printed manager or general partner. Recorded once on the document row, not repeated on every observation.
The printed asset owner, verbatim as the page renders it. Recorded once on the document row.
The printed portfolio or programme the document reports on. Recorded once on the document row.
The printed vintage year of the fund on that row.
The printed start of the period the value covers.
The printed end of the period the value covers.
The printed date the value is stated as of, in the fullest printed form. December 31, 2015, not 2015, and never reformatted to ISO.
The printed measurement period for a return or risk figure, such as 1-Yr, 5 Year, ITD, or Fiscal YTD 9 Months. Required whenever the column header carries a period qualifier.
The printed currency and scale statement that makes the number readable, such as $ in millions, copied verbatim including any parentheses.
What the value measures, chosen from the one metric vocabulary by the printed meaning; the family says where the cell sat, the category says what it is. This is the field the database joins on.

The printed label for the measure, taken from whichever axis names it: the row label where rows are measures and columns are periods, the leaf column header where rows are entities and columns are measures, and the table's own title only where neither axis names a measure. Never a section heading, and never identical to horizon. The page's own wording, not a controlled value.
The printed value, copied verbatim: currency symbol, thousands separators, decimals, sign, and parentheses all preserved. Never calculated, rounded, rescaled, or repunctuated.
The unit of measure printed for the value: %, x, bps, years, shares. A currency is never a unit; it belongs in currency_scale.
For provisions only: which term of the one term vocabulary the clause states, such as management_fee or key_person.
For legal provisions and qualitative facts: the printed wording of the provision.
For legal provisions: the printed basis a rate or amount is calculated on, such as committed capital.
For legal provisions: the printed condition or qualification attached to the term.
One short line copied verbatim from the cited page that contains the value. Checked against the page, so it cannot be paraphrased.
Whether the value is an actual reported figure, an illustrative or template figure, a stated requirement, a definition, or redacted.
Free-text remarks. Also carries the NO_ELIGIBLE_REASON and IMAGE_ONLY prefixes where the field list requires them.
On a final adjudicated row, which extractors the fact came from: A, B, A+B, or ADJUDICATOR.
On a final adjudicated row, how it was settled: AGREED, VERIFIED_ONE_SIDED, RESOLVED, or ADDED.
On a definition_context row, the printed marker the note is keyed by; on a value row, the pipe-joined printed markers citing the definitions that govern it.
evidence: SRC063 p1 footnotes; SRC457 p2 footnotes 1-4

output_value: How a return was computed, from the page's own statement: time_weighted, money_weighted, modified_dietz, simple_period, annualized, actuarial, or unstated.
The fee treatment the page states for the value: net, gross, partial, or unstated.
The grain the page states for a value: fund_position, single_holding, portfolio_total, plan_total, statement_line, allocation_bucket, or unstated.
The printed industry or economic sector of the subject; it remains separate from the fund's asset class and strategy.
